newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL-ITALY CLASH ILLUMINATES TOURNOI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL-ITALY CLASH ILLUMINATES TOURNOI.

text.p: Brazil and Italy, who have seven World Cups between them and have met in two finals, clash in one of the most eagerly-awaited matches of the Tournoi de France on Sunday.
Their confrontation is being billed as a rematch of their Los Angeles showdown in the World Cup final three years ago won by the Brazilians on penalties.

Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said a revenge match was only possible in a World Cup, but he and his players are as keen to win this match a year before the 1998 finals in France as much as the Italians might want to avenge the 1994 defeat.
"It's a great match because of the ambiance, the tradition, the two have played so many big games, like the final in 1970," Paris St Germain midfielder Leonardo said.
"We want to win because it's important to win the tournament," he added, referring to this dress rehearsal organised by 1998 World Cup hosts France.
Brazil will field six from the side that played in the 1994 World Cup final, if they are unchanged from Tuesday's 1-1 draw with the hosts which is Zagallo's intention.
Goalkeeper Taffarel, defenders Cafu -- as a substitute for Jorginho -- and Aldair, midfielders Mauro Silva and Dunga and striker Romario all played for the winners in the 1994 final.

But the Brazilians had two injury scares, with Romario feeing the effects of a previous groin strain and needing rest rather than training on Thursday, while Taffarel twisted his ankle in a practice and is doubtful.
The Italians, ironically due to injury problems, could line up as many as five survivors of 1994.
From their Tournoi squad, Paolo Maldini, now captain, left back Antonio Benarrivo, midfielders Demetrio Albertini and Dino Baggio and goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca all played for Italy in Los Angeles.

Italy, bottom of the Tournoi table after their 2-0 loss to England on Wednesday, came to France depleted by injuries and are without Roberto Baggio, who inspired them to the 1994 final only to miss a crucial penalty in the U.S. shootout.
With Chelsea's Roberto Di Matteo nursing a knock on the knee against England and Giampiero Maini of Vicenza doubtful with a pulled hamstring, Dino Baggio could claim a place in midfield.
Angelo Peruzzi of Juventus is Italy's first choice 'keeper but if coach Cesare Maldini decides to rest several players, Pagliuca could make a comeback after two years out of the picture.
"I'll be glad for him if he gets the chance and I hope to be there too," Taffarel said.
The elder Maldini has more injury woes since the match against England, also Italy's rivals in World Cup qualifiers, with Juventus defender Ciro Ferrera out with a serious groin strain.

Asked how he thought young central defender Fabio Cannavaro would cope with Brazil's formidable striker Ronaldo, Maldini said: "You may say he lacks experience but if you don't play you don't get experience. He has already come up against (Alan) Shearer at Wembley."
Brazil and Italy have met 10 times since 1956 with the Brazilians winning five times and the Italians four. The only draw was in the 1994 World Cup final. The goals tally is 15-14 in Brazil's favour.
Teams:
Brazil - Taffarel; Cafu, Celio Silva, Aldair, Roberto Carlos; Giovanni, Mauro Silva, Dunga, Leonardo; Ronaldo, Romario.

Italy (probable) - Angelo Peruzzi; Christian Panucci, Fabio Cannavaro, Paolo Maldini, Antonio Benarrivo; Angelo Di Livio, Diego Fuser, Dino Baggio, Roberto Di Matteo; Alessandro Del Piero, Pierluigi Casiraghi.
Referee: Serge Muhmenthaler (Switzerland).
